message.content: {"key_mechanism_gt": "The detailed catalytic cycle in nickel-metallaphotoredox systems involves a specific sequence of single-electron transfers and radical recombination steps that dictate the chemo-, regio-, and stereo-selectivity of C(sp³)-C(sp³) and C(sp³)-C(sp²) bond formation.", "key_mechanism_gen": "The steric bulk of the NHC ligand creates a kinetic bottleneck that favors the rapid capture of the sp3 radical by the Ni(II) species over side reactions, while the electron-withdrawing nature of the NHC modulates the redox potential of the nickel center to facilitate smooth electron transfer from the photoredox catalyst without leading to irreversible decomposition of the alkyl-nickel intermediate.", "recovery": "PARTIAL", "rationale": "The generated hypothesis focuses on steric and electronic effects of NHC ligands to suppress side reactions and stabilize intermediates, while the ground truth emphasizes the sequence of single-electron transfers and radical recombination as the core mechanism dictating selectivity."}
